headline: Leaning lower, with big swings likely
text: US futures are down ahead of the open (S&P −0.64%, Nasdaq −1.55%).
Helping: S&P 500 vs 200-day, Stocks above 200-day. Weighing: 10-year yield, Copper.
Expect a jumpy session: SPY options gamma is negative (dealers' hedging makes moves bigger). Gaps and reversals are common in these conditions, so a small early move says little.
Tomorrow brings Retail sales, so traders may hold back today.
Options price a typical day of about ±1.1% for the S&P 500 (about 7,428–7,599); historically about 82% of days stay inside that.

On past days with VIX between 15 and 20 and the VIX curve normal (since 1990, 1,618 days), the next session closed higher 54% of the time (all days: 54%), with a typical move of 0.5% (all days: 0.5%).

drivers.name: US futures
drivers.note: S&P −0.64% · Nasdaq −1.55% vs the last close. The clearest hint of how the day opens.

drivers.name: 10-year yield
drivers.note: At 5.15%. Fast-rising yields hurt growth and tech stocks; falling yields help them.

drivers.name: WTI oil
drivers.note: $88.97. A big oil jump feeds inflation worries; energy stocks move with it.

drivers.name: Gold
drivers.note: $3876. A strong gold bid often means investors are looking for safety.

drivers.name: Copper
drivers.note: “Dr. Copper”: rising copper = traders expect more growth.

drivers.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day
drivers.note: Above the 200-day = long-term uptrend: dips have tended to get bought.

drivers.name: Stocks above 200-day
drivers.note: How many big US stocks are in their own uptrend.

drivers.name: VIX
drivers.note: Below 16 calm, above 25 nervous, above 30 fear.

drivers.name: VIX curve
drivers.note: Normal (below 1): no panic in the options market.

drivers.name: Market mood
drivers.note: Neutral: the site's 0–100 fear/greed gauge from 10 readings. Extremes often mark turning points, so it sets the tone rather than the direction.

levels.name: SPY call wall
levels.note: Biggest call position: often acts as a ceiling.

levels.name: SPY gamma flip
levels.note: Above it dealers calm moves down; below it they speed them up.

levels.name: SPY put wall
levels.note: Biggest put position: often acts as a floor; a break can speed up selling.

levels.name: SPY call wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new call trading is concentrated: shows the ceiling shifting during the session.

levels.name: SPY put wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new put trading is concentrated: shows the floor shifting during the session.

base.label: VIX between 15 and 20 and the VIX curve normal

scenarios.text: Above 755 (put wall) is where rallies often stall.
Yesterday's S&P 500 range was 7,499–7,622: a break of either end is the first real sign of direction.

tips: Size smaller than usual and use the “wrong if” level on every alert.
